pr.title: Mention project ios in the AGENTS.md template
pr.head: a03fbce4990414705c382e6d19b1059267bdf062

summary: project init writes a block of Projector conventions into every adopting repository's AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Every agent session in that repository reads it, whether or not the Projector plugin is installed. Until this change the block said nothing about project ios, the command that builds a branch or a pull request of an iOS app in a worktree of its own and installs it on a device. The steps for a device test lived only in the implement skill, which an agent reads only inside Projector's own flows.
This change adds two paragraphs to the template, both scoped to a repository with an iOS app:

• A general paragraph. It applies with or without the plugin. It says to build and install through project ios rather than xcodebuild or devicectl, never to pass --allow-untrusted yourself, to build with --no-install and install on the person's device only when they ask, which commands the person runs on their own Mac, and how to get crash reports and device logs.
  • A plugin paragraph. It sits under "Projector skills" after the rule about a request's start action. It points at the implement skill's "Prepare a device test for an iOS app" and keeps one rule: build with --no-install before posting the request, and install only in the start action.
The template's version moves from 27 to 28, the test that pins each version's hash gains the new one, and this repository's own AGENTS.md is refreshed to the new block.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, of 878f3d7, requested changes with one finding: the general paragraph sent agents to project ios build, which installs by default, without saying to install on the person's device only when they ask. It also suggested matching the implement skill's crash and log advice.
  • a03fbce adds the --no-install rule to the general paragraph and adopts the skill's crash and log wording. Its review is clean, and its one suggestion is to update the pull request body, which still describes the first head's paragraph.
  • The full test suite, project check, and git diff --check passed on both heads.

groups.title: The conventions template
groups.kicker: Two new paragraphs about project ios, and the version that marks the change
intro: The template is the single source of the block. Its first line, <!-- projector:begin 28 -->, carries the version that project check compares against a repository's copy, so an older copy is reported as stale.

Read the general paragraph as an agent without the plugin would. That agent follows only the general conventions, so the rule to build with --no-install and install on the person's device only when they ask sits there, not only under "Projector skills".

checks.text: Every command and flag the paragraphs name exists in the ios parser in cli.py: build with --no-install and --allow-untrusted, install with --device, crashes, and logs. Checked by reading the parser at the head.

files.note: The template project init renders into each repository. The version bumps and two iOS paragraphs are added.

checks.text: This sentence keeps an agent without the plugin from installing unasked: project ios build installs and opens the app unless you pass --no-install. No other command the block tells an agent to run installs on its own, and project ios install runs only in a request's start action. Checked by reading the ios parser in cli.py and build in ios.py.

The crash and log advice now matches the implement skill: crashes --device <udid> for the device the person tested on, and otherwise a request that the person run crashes or logs and share the file. Checked by reading both texts side by side.

This paragraph matches the implement skill's steps: push, build with --no-install before posting the request, and run project ios install <number> --device <udid> only after STARTED. Checked by reading both texts side by side.

groups.title: This repository's copy and the pinned hash
groups.kicker: The rendered block and the test that keeps the template's version honest
intro: Projector adopts its own conventions, so its AGENTS.md carries the rendered block, and CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it. A test pins a SHA-256 hash of the template text for each version, so editing the text without bumping the version fails the suite. Version 28 has not reached the default branch, so the second head changes its text in place and pins the new hash rather than bumping to 29.

checks.text: AGENTS.md contains instructions.render("docs/projects") exactly, the template's hash equals the pinned hash for version 28, and CLAUDE.md is still a symlink to AGENTS.md. Checked by rendering the template and hashing it at the head, and by running tests.test_instructions.

files.note: The refreshed block, identical to the rendered template.
